summary: We developed a Smart Health Monitoring System for Astronauts to continuously track and monitor the health conditions of astronauts during space missions. The system monitors important vital signs such as heart rate, body temperature, blood oxygen level (SpO₂), and blood pressure using health sensors. The collected data is displayed on a real-time dashboard, allowing astronauts and mission control teams to monitor health conditions remotely. The system can detect abnormal readings and generate instant alerts when vital signs exceed predefined safety limits. It also maintains health records to help identify potential medical issues early. This project addresses the challenges of limited medical facilities, delayed medical assistance, and health risks in space environments. It is important because astronauts experience extreme conditions such as microgravity, isolation, and radiation, which can affect their physical health. Our solution helps ensure astronaut safety, supports early medical intervention, and improves the success of long-duration space missions.
details:
1. What does the project do and how does it work?

Our project, Astronaut Health Monitoring System, is designed to monitor the physical health of astronauts during space missions. It continuously tracks important health parameters such as heart rate, body temperature, blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂), and blood pressure.

The system collects health information through sensors and sends the readings to a monitoring dashboard. The dashboard displays the collected data in real time, allowing astronauts and mission control teams to observe changes in health conditions. If any parameter crosses its predefined safety threshold, the system generates an alert so that appropriate action can be taken.

2. What are the benefits of the project?

  • Enables continuous monitoring of astronauts' vital signs.
  • Helps identify unusual health conditions at an early stage.
  • Provides quick alerts when abnormal readings are detected.
  • Allows mission control teams to monitor astronauts remotely.
  • Maintains health records for tracking changes over time.
  • Reduces dependence on manual health checks.

3. What is the intended impact?

The main objective is to improve astronaut safety and support healthier, longer-duration space missions. Astronauts experience unique challenges such as microgravity, radiation exposure, isolation, and limited access to medical facilities. Our system aims to provide continuous health information and early warnings, helping astronauts and medical teams make informed decisions. In the future, it could support personalized health monitoring and predictive analysis for space exploration missions.

4. What tools, programming languages, hardware, and software were used?

Our proposed development technologies include:

  • Programming languages: Python, JavaScript, and HTML/CSS.
  • Frontend: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the monitoring dashboard.
  • Backend: Python for processing health data and generating alerts.
  • Hardware: ESP32 or Arduino microcontroller.
  • Sensors: Heart-rate sensor, MAX30102 pulse oximeter, and body-temperature sensor.
  • Database: Firebase or MySQL for storing health records.
  • Development tools: Visual Studio Code and Arduino IDE.

5. How is the project creative and innovative?

The creativity of our project lies in combining multiple health-monitoring parameters into a single monitoring platform specifically designed for space missions. Instead of checking individual health measurements separately, the system provides a unified dashboard with real-time readings, health status indicators, and automatic alerts. It can also be extended with artificial intelligence and machine learning to identify unusual health patterns and predict potential health risks.

6. What factors did our team consider?

Our team considered several important factors while designing the system:

  • Accuracy: Health sensors should provide reliable measurements.
  • Real-time monitoring: Health information should be updated continuously.
  • Reliability: The system should operate consistently during long-duration missions.
  • Low power consumption: Hardware should use minimal energy.
  • Data security: Astronauts' medical information must remain confidential.
  • User-friendly interface: Information should be easy to understand.
  • Communication: Health information should be transmitted securely to mission control.
  • Scalability: The system should support future improvements and additional health parameters.

Conclusion

The Astronaut Health Monitoring System is a technology-driven solution aimed at making space missions safer by providing continuous health monitoring, early detection of abnormal conditions, and remote health-data access. Our vision is to contribute to safer human space exploration through accessible, reliable, and intelligent health-monitoring technology.
